content:
With AI agents rapidly rising and a flood of requests seeking full disk access on Mac, Apple says it will make changes to macOS to protect user privacy.

Although Apple has not disclosed the specific details, it stated that users should understand what it really means to grant such 'extremely high' permissions to applications.

In a blog post on its Developer website, Apple explained that full disk access in macOS was originally designed to 'let backup apps work properly on Mac'. However, Apple noted that 'some developers' are using macOS's full disk access settings in ways that 'could put users at risk'.

Apple said it will 'introduce additional safeguards to ensure that users who truly intend to grant an app this extremely high level of access must do so through a very clear user action'.

The company did not reveal further details about these safeguards or the specific changes. However, Apple said that the rise of 'increasingly capable and autonomous' AI agents demands greater attention to privacy and security:

Apple's announcement comes as tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots become increasingly popular. These always-on AI agents request access to large amounts of personal data, and we have already seen some alarming cases involving Meta Muse.
